newsitem.title: USA: Most corporate treasurers expect cost cuts.
newsitem.headline: Most corporate treasurers expect cost cuts.

text.p: Seventy percent of corporate treasurers and cash management executives said aggressive cost cutting will continue at their companies next year, a survey said.
The survey of 334 people interviewed face-to-face was conducted for American Express by Louis Harris & Associates at the annual Treasury Management Association conference in Atlanta this week.
Forty-five percent of those interviewed said their companies had specific goals for cutting costs in 1997.

Of that group, 11 percent said costs at their company would by slashed by 10 percent to 25 percent, 34 percent said costs would be reduced by 5 percent to 10 percent and 32 percent said the target would be 1 percent to 5 percent.
Although most companies found benefits through cost cutting, two out of 10 said their company experienced serious drawbacks from cost cutting, including morale problems and staffing shortages.
